# Book II, Proposition 4

*The squares on the whole and both segments*

[Euclid's proof](#euclids-proof) · [In Lean](#in-lean) · [What it rests on](#what-it-rests-on) · [Mishnah](#mishnah)

> If a straight line be cut at random, the square on the whole is equal to the squares on the segments and twice the rectangle contained by the segments.

**In Lean:** ✅ proved, as Euclid states it · Euclid's argument

<p align="center"><em>Cut AB anywhere, at C (red, blue), and the square on AB splits into the squares on AC, CB (red, blue) and two rectangles contained by AC, CB (yellow).</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/II/04.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition II.4, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

For let the straight line AB be cut at random at C;

I say that the square on AB is equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle contained by AC, CB.

For let the square ADEB be described on AB, [I. 46]

let BD be joined;

through C let CF be drawn parallel to either AD or EB,

and through G let HK be drawn parallel to either AB or DE. [I. 31]

Then, since CF is parallel to AD,

and BD has fallen on them,

the exterior angle CGB is equal to the interior and opposite angle ADB. [I. 29]

But the angle ADB is equal to the angle ABD,

since the side BA is also equal to AD; [I. 5]

therefore the angle CGB is also equal to the angle GBC,

so that the side BC is also equal to the side CG. [I. 6]

But CB is equal to GK, and CG to KB; [I. 34]

therefore GK is also equal to KB;

therefore CGKB is equilateral.

I say next that it is also right-angled.

For, since CG is parallel to BK,

the angles KBC, GCB are equal to two right angles. [I. 29]

But the angle KBC is right;

therefore the angle BCG is also right,

so that the opposite angles CGK, GKB are also right. [I. 34]

Therefore CGKB is right-angled;

and it was also proved equilateral;

therefore it is a square;

and it is described on CB.

For the same reason

HF is also a square;

and it is described on HG, that is AC. [I. 34]

Therefore the squares HF, KC are the squares on AC, CB.

Now, since AG is equal to GE,

and AG is the rectangle AC, CB, for GC is equal to CB,

therefore GE is also equal to the rectangle AC, CB.

Therefore AG, GE are equal to twice the rectangle AC, CB.

But the squares HF, CK are also the squares on AC, CB;

therefore the four areas HF, CK, AG, GE are equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle contained by AC, CB.

But HF, CK, AG, GE are the whole ADEB,

which is the square on AB.

Therefore the square on AB is equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle contained by AC, CB.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

**How the Lean follows the text**

- **Carried together, by `Square.about_diameter`.** "For the same reason…" Euclid's "for the same reason" is carried by one lemma, which gives his argument for CK over any letters: a parallelogram about the diameter of a square is a square.

```lean
/-- If a straight line be cut at random, the square on the whole is equal to the squares on the
segments and twice the rectangle contained by the segments. -/
theorem Prop4 {A B C : Point} (hACB : Between A C B) :
    sq A B = sq A C + sq C B + (rect A C C B + rect A C C B) := by
  -- For let the straight line AB be cut at random at C;
  have hAB : A ≠ B := ne_of_between_ends hACB
  have hBCA : Between B C A := between_symm hACB
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  have hC_AB : OnLine C AB := on_line_of_between_ends hACB hA_AB hB_AB
  -- I say that the square on AB is equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle
  -- contained by AC, CB.
  -- For let the square ADEB be described on AB, [I. 46]
  obtain ⟨P, hP, -⟩ := exists_off_line hAB []
  obtain ⟨D, E, hsq, hD, hE⟩ := BookI.Prop46 hAB hP
  obtain ⟨hp, hADEB⟩ := Square.described hsq hD hE
  -- let BD be joined;
  have hBADE : Parallelogram B A D E := hp.rotate.rotate.rotate
  have hBD : B ≠ D := hBADE.triangle.ne₁₃
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hBD
  -- through C let CF be drawn parallel to either AD or EB,
  -- and through G let HK be drawn parallel to either AB or DE. [I. 31]
  /- G is where CF cuts BD; F, H, K are where the parallels meet the sides. -/
  obtain ⟨F, G, H, K, hBGD, hDFE, hAHD, hEKB, hCGF, -, hBCGK, hGHDF⟩ := hp.figure hACB
  -- Then, since CF is parallel to AD,
  obtain ⟨AD, hA_AD, hD_AD⟩ := Postulate1 A D hp.1.1
  obtain ⟨CF, hC_CF, hF_CF⟩ := Postulate1 C F (ne_of_between_ends hCGF)
  have hG_CF : OnLine G CF := on_line_of_between_ends hCGF hC_CF hF_CF
  have hH_AD : OnLine H AD := on_line_of_between_ends hAHD hA_AD hD_AD
  have hCF_AD : Parallel CF AD := (hGHDF.2.parallel hH_AD hD_AD hF_CF hG_CF).symm
  have hGC_DA : AreParallel G C D A :=
    AreParallel.of_parallel (ne_of_between hCGF).symm hp.1.1.symm hG_CF hC_CF hD_AD hA_AD hCF_AD
  -- and BD has fallen on them,
  have hG_BD : OnLine G BD := on_line_of_between_ends hBGD hB_BD hD_BD
  have hGD : G ≠ D := ne_of_between (between_symm hBGD) |>.symm
  have hC_BD : ¬ OnLine C BD := fun h =>
    hBADE.triangle.off_line hB_BD ((line_unique (ne_of_between hBCA) hB_AB hC_AB hB_BD h) ▸ hA_AB) hD_BD
  have hCA : SameSideOf C A G D :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hGD hG_BD hD_BD (pasch2 hBCA hB_BD hC_BD)
  -- the exterior angle CGB is equal to the interior and opposite angle ADB. [I. 29]
  have h29 : ∠ B G C = ∠ G D A := BookI.Prop29.exterior hGC_DA hCA hBGD
  have hGB : G ≠ B := (ne_of_between hBGD).symm
  have hCG : C ≠ G := ne_of_between hCGF
  have hCB : C ≠ B := (ne_of_between hBCA).symm
  have hAD : A ≠ D := hp.1.1
  have hCGB : ∠ C G B = ∠ A D B := by
    rw [angle_symm hCG hGB.symm, h29, angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hBGD)) hAD,
      angle_symm hBD hAD]
  -- But the angle ADB is equal to the angle ABD,
  -- since the side BA is also equal to AD; [I. 5]
  have h5 : ∠ A D B = ∠ A B D :=
    BookI.Prop5.base hBADE.triangle.bac.acb hsq.len_eq.symm
  -- therefore the angle CGB is also equal to the angle GBC,
  have hGBC : ∠ C G B = ∠ G B C := by
    rw [hCGB, h5, angle_eq_of_onRay (OnRay.of_between hBGD) (OnRay.of_between hBCA),
      angle_symm hAB hBD.symm]
  -- so that the side BC is also equal to the side CG. [I. 6]
  have hBC_CG : ‖C B‖ = ‖C G‖ := by
    have hCBG : Triangle C B G := hBCGK.triangle.bac
    exact BookI.Prop6 hCBG (by rw [angle_symm hCB hGB]; exact hGBC.symm)
  -- But CB is equal to GK, and CG to KB; [I. 34]
  obtain ⟨hCB_GK, hCG_BK, -, -, -⟩ :=
    BookI.Prop34 (A := C) (B := B) (C := G) (D := K) hBCGK.rotate
  -- therefore GK is also equal to KB;
  have hGK_KB : ‖G K‖ = ‖K B‖ := by
    rw [← hCB_GK, hBC_CG, hCG_BK, len_symm B K]
  -- therefore CGKB is equilateral.
  have hequil : ‖C G‖ = ‖G K‖ ∧ ‖G K‖ = ‖K B‖ ∧ ‖K B‖ = ‖B C‖ :=
    ⟨hBC_CG.symm.trans hCB_GK, hGK_KB,
      hGK_KB.symm.trans (hCB_GK.symm.trans (len_symm C B))⟩
  -- I say next that it is also right-angled.
  -- For, since CG is parallel to BK,
  -- the angles KBC, GCB are equal to two right angles. [I. 29]
  have h29' : ∠ K B C + ∠ B C G = ∟ + ∟ :=
    BookI.Prop29.interior hBCGK.2.symm.swap_left hBCGK.sameSideOf.symm
  -- But the angle KBC is right;
  have hKBC : ∠ K B C = ∟ := by
    rw [angle_eq_of_onRay (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hEKB)) (OnRay.of_between hBCA)]
    exact hsq.2.2.2.2.2.2
  -- therefore the angle BCG is also right,
  have hBCG : ∠ B C G = ∟ := by
    rw [hKBC, add_comm] at h29'
    exact CommonNotion3 h29' rfl
  -- so that the opposite angles CGK, GKB are also right. [I. 34]
  obtain ⟨-, -, hGCB_GKB, hCBK_CGK, -⟩ :=
    BookI.Prop34 (A := C) (B := B) (C := G) (D := K) hBCGK.rotate
  have hCGK : ∠ C G K = ∟ := by
    rw [← hCBK_CGK, angle_symm hCB (ne_of_between (between_symm hEKB)).symm]; exact hKBC
  have hGKB : ∠ G K B = ∟ := hGCB_GKB ▸ hBCG
  -- Therefore CGKB is right-angled;
  have hright : ∠ B C G = ∟ ∧ ∠ C G K = ∟ ∧ ∠ G K B = ∟ ∧ ∠ K B C = ∟ :=
    ⟨hBCG, hCGK, hGKB, hKBC⟩
  -- and it was also proved equilateral;
  -- therefore it is a square;
  have hCK : Square C G K B := ⟨hequil.1, hequil.2.1, hequil.2.2, hright⟩
  -- and it is described on CB.
  have hsq₁ : quadArea B C G K = sq C B := by
    rw [← hBCGK.quadArea_rotate, hCK.eq_sq hBCGK.rotate, sq_congr hBC_CG.symm]
  -- For the same reason
  -- HF is also a square;
  have hHF : Square D F G H :=
    hsq.rotate.about_diameter hp.rotate (between_symm hBGD) hDFE (between_symm hAHD)
      hGHDF.rotate.rotate
  -- and it is described on HG, that is AC. [I. 34]
  obtain ⟨hCAHG, -⟩ := hBADE.complements hBGD hBCA hAHD hDFE hEKB hBCGK hGHDF
  have hsq₂ : quadArea G H D F = sq A C := by
    rw [← quadArea_rotate₂ G H D F, hHF.eq_sq hGHDF.rotate.rotate]
    obtain ⟨-, hCA_GH, -, -, -⟩ := BookI.Prop34 (A := C) (B := G) (C := A) (D := H) hCAHG
    exact sq_congr ((hHF.1.trans hHF.2.1).trans (hCA_GH.symm.trans (len_symm C A)))
  -- Therefore the squares HF, KC are the squares on AC, CB.
  have hsquares : quadArea G H D F + quadArea B C G K = sq A C + sq C B := by
    rw [hsq₂, hsq₁]
  -- Now, since AG is equal to GE,
  have h43 : quadArea C A H G = quadArea K G F E :=
    BookI.Prop43 hBADE hBGD hBCA hAHD hDFE hEKB hBCGK hGHDF
  -- and AG is the rectangle AC, CB, for GC is equal to CB,
  have hAG : quadArea C A H G = rect A C C B := by
    have hG_AB : ¬ OnLine G AB := fun hG =>
      (hBCGK.triangle).off_line hB_AB hC_AB hG
    have hright : ∠ G C A = ∟ := by
      have h := hBCG
      rw [adjacent_eq_of_right hB_AB hA_AB hBCA hG_AB h] at h
      exact h
    exact (Rectangle.of_right hCAHG hright).eq_rect (len_symm C A) hBC_CG.symm
  -- therefore GE is also equal to the rectangle AC, CB.
  have hGE : quadArea K G F E = rect A C C B := h43 ▸ hAG
  -- Therefore AG, GE are equal to twice the rectangle AC, CB.
  have hrectangles : quadArea C A H G + quadArea K G F E = rect A C C B + rect A C C B := by
    rw [hAG, hGE]
  -- But the squares HF, CK are also the squares on AC, CB;
  -- therefore the four areas HF, CK, AG, GE are equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the
  -- rectangle contained by AC, CB.
  have hfour : quadArea G H D F + quadArea B C G K +
      (quadArea C A H G + quadArea K G F E) =
      sq A C + sq C B + (rect A C C B + rect A C C B) := by
    rw [hsquares, hrectangles]
  -- But HF, CK, AG, GE are the whole ADEB,
  have hwhole := hBADE.about_diameter hBGD hBCA hAHD hDFE hEKB hBCGK hGHDF
  -- which is the square on AB.
  have hsqAB : quadArea B A D E = sq A B := hBADE.quadArea_rotate.symm.trans hADEB
  -- Therefore the square on AB is equal to the squares on AC, CB and twice the rectangle
  -- contained by AC, CB.
  calc
    sq A B = quadArea B A D E := hsqAB.symm
    _ = quadArea B C G K + quadArea C A H G + quadArea G H D F + quadArea K G F E := hwhole
    _ = quadArea G H D F + quadArea B C G K + (quadArea C A H G + quadArea K G F E) := by ac_rfl
    _ = sq A C + sq C B + (rect A C C B + rect A C C B) := hfour
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.
```

- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L111) (used here): If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L114) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.figure`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L299), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200) and 4 other lemmas): A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L119) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.figure`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L299), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200) and 4 other lemmas): If two different straight lines L and M meet at B, and A and C are points of M, different from each other and from B, that are not on the same side of L, then B is between A and C. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L99) (through [`Square.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L134)): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L85) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.figure`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L299), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200) and 3 other lemmas): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L89) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.figure`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L299), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200) and 6 other lemmas): If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side as A. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L96) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.figure`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L299), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200) and 4 other lemmas): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L131) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200), [`Rectangle.eq_rect`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L98) and 3 other lemmas): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A. If C lies within the angle BAD (on D's side of L and on B's side of N), then B and D are not on the same side of M: the straight line AC separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L139): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A, with B other than A and D off M. If C and D are on the same side of L, and B and D are not on the same side of M, then B and C are on the same side of N: C lies within the angle BAD. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`adjacent_eq_of_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L67) (used here): A right angle is equal to the angle adjacent to it. (Diagram-angle 3; the other half is Definition 10 together with Postulate 4)
- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54): If D lies within the angle BAC, then BAC is made up of BAD and DAC. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L72) (through [`BookI.Prop29.exterior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L160), [`Square.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L134), [`angle_eq_of_onRay`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L31) and 1 other lemma): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26) (used here): The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4)
- [`area_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L88) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200), [`Rectangle.eq_rect`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L98) and 2 other lemmas): Cutting a triangle in two from a vertex adds up. (Diagram-area 2)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_degenerate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L32) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200), [`Rectangle.eq_rect`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L98) and 2 other lemmas): A "triangle" with a repeated corner has no area. (Metric 6)
- [`area_eq_zero_of_on_line`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L80) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200), [`Rectangle.eq_rect`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L98) and 2 other lemmas): A "triangle" whose corners lie on one straight line has no area. (Diagram-area 1)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200), [`Rectangle.eq_rect`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L98) and 3 other lemmas): The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200), [`Rectangle.eq_rect`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L98) and 2 other lemmas): The triangle ABC is the triangle ACB. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17) (through [`Rectangle.eq_rect`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L98), [`Square.described`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L113), [`Square.eq_sq`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L106) and 1 other lemma): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L33): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L21) (through [`exists_off_line`](../../Elements/Figure/Rectangles.lean#L39)): If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L37): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23) (used here): The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3)
- [`on_line_of_area_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L84): A triangle with no area has its corners on one straight line. (Diagram-area 1)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L49): If the angle BAC is nothing, C lies on the ray from A through B. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle ABC can be applied to the straight line L with A on D, B on the ray from D through G, and C on the side of L where H is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L23) (through [`Magnitude.instAssociative`](../../Elements/Figure/Areas.lean#L33), [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200) and 3 other lemmas): Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last two are added first. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26) (used here): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29) (through [`Parallelogram.about_diameter`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L225), [`Parallelogram.quadArea_rotate`](../../Elements/Figure/Parallelograms.lean#L200), [`Rectangle.eq_rect`](../../Elements/BookII/Rectangles.lean#L98) and 2 other lemmas): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32) (through [`exists_off_line`](../../Elements/Figure/Rectangles.lean#L39)): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39) (through [`exists_off_line`](../../Elements/Figure/Rectangles.lean#L39)): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42) (through [`exists_off_line`](../../Elements/Figure/Rectangles.lean#L39)): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

_Our commentary: what Euclid assumes, what Lean made us say out loud, and how the result looks by modern means._

**"Shown in the figures."** Euclid cuts the square on AB into four pieces with the diameter BD, his word for a diagonal, and the parallels CF and HK: two squares, and two complements equal to one another. His HK goes "through G", a point he never introduces: it is where CF crosses BD, a meeting we prove. Heath sees the whole book in this: "It is important however to bear in mind that the whole procedure of Book II. is *geometrical*; rectangles and squares are shown in the figures, and the equality of certain combinations to other combinations is proved by those figures" (vol. 1, p. 373). [Book II's introduction](index.md#areas) reads our areas off this figure, piece by piece.

**"I say next that it is also right-angled."** Euclid proves CGKB a square in full, down to every right angle, and our proof follows him. One step goes unnamed in his text: taking the right angle KBC from two right angles, to leave the angle BCG right, is Common Notion 3. The proof attributed to Theon stops at the right angle at B, "a legitimate abbreviation of the genuine proof", Heath says (vol. 1, p. 381), since I.46 has already shown that when one angle of such a figure is right, all are.

**"For the same reason."** With these words Euclid makes HF a square too, without repeating the argument. The Greek text also has a Porism that says it in general, which Heath calls "undoubtedly interpolated": "From this it is manifest that in square areas the parallelograms about the diameter are squares" (vol. 1, p. 381). J. L. Heiberg suspected Theon, and a papyrus fragment lacks it. Euclid's reason holds for any square, so we prove it in general, as `Square.about_diameter`, and use it here for HF and again in II.5 to II.8.

**"Twice the rectangle."** Heath gives no bracket for "AG is equal to GE": it is I.43, on the complements. Each complement is the rectangle AC, CB, so the two are twice it, and Heath notes: "By a curious idiom this is in Greek 'the rectangle *twice contained* by the segments'" (vol. 1, p. 380). The semi-algebraical proof, from II.2 and then II.3 twice, Heath finds in Christopher Clavius and most later editions (vol. 1, p. 381).

**The modern way.** With AC = a and CB = b, II.4 is (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab. For vectors, |u + v|² = |u|² + |v|² + 2u·v, and AC and CB point the same way, so for them u·v is ab.

## Further reading

- For the vector form, |u + v|² = |u|² + |v|² + 2u·v, John Stillwell's [*The Four Pillars of Geometry*](https://doi.org/10.1007/0-387-29052-4) (2005), ch. 4, "Vectors and Euclidean spaces", where the dot product arrives.
- For Book II read as squares and rectangles shown in the figures, as Heath reminds us it is, David Fowler's [*The Mathematics of Plato's Academy*](https://academic.oup.com/book/52809) (1999), ch. 3, "Elements II: The Dimension of Squares", a bold reading of the book without our algebra.
